title: Copy-on-Write Snapshots
description: Creates instant snapshots that share unchanged blocks with the live filesystem. Only modified blocks consume new space, so snapshots are nearly free to create. ZFS and btrfs made this the standard for filesystem time travel.

demo.title: Demo — Copy-on-Write Snapshots

title: Event Sourcing
description: Rebuilds application state by replaying the immutable event log. Instead of storing current state, the system stores every change; state is a fold over events. Any past state is recoverable by replaying to a point.
key_mechanisms: Append every change as an event

demo.title: Demo — Event Sourcing

title: CRDT State Merge
description: Merges divergent replicas without coordination using conflict-free replicated data types. Each replica snapshots locally and merges mathematically, guaranteeing convergence. It powers collaborative editing and offline-first apps.

demo.title: Demo — CRDT State Merge

title: VM Snapshots
description: Captures memory, disk, and device state of a virtual machine for instant rollback. A snapshot freezes the whole machine; restore returns to the exact moment. It is the safety net under every risky upgrade.

demo.title: Demo — VM Snapshots

title: Container Checkpoint/Restore
description: Uses CRIU to freeze running containers and restore them elsewhere, even on another host. Process trees, memory, and open files are captured and revived. It enables live migration and instant startup from checkpoints.
key_mechanisms: Freeze the process tree with CRIU

demo.title: Demo — Container Checkpoint/Restore

title: Database Point-in-Time Recovery
description: Replays the write-ahead log to restore the database to any point in time. Base backup plus WAL replay gives second-granularity recovery. It is how databases survive both disasters and bad migrations.

demo.title: Demo — Database Point-in-Time Recovery

title: Filesystem Snapshots
description: Schedules periodic filesystem snapshots with retention policies for routine time travel. Hourly, daily, and weekly snapshots give users self-service restore of deleted files. Retention bounds the storage cost.

demo.title: Demo — Filesystem Snapshots

title: Application Memento
description: Implements the memento pattern so application state supports undo and restore points. The originator captures state into opaque mementos; a caretaker manages them. It is the classic undo mechanism, generalized.
key_mechanisms: Restore by handing back a memento

demo.title: Demo — Application Memento

title: Distributed Consistent Snapshots
description: Applies the Chandy-Lamport algorithm for globally consistent cuts across distributed processes. Marker messages separate pre- and post-snapshot events so the captured state could actually have occurred. It underpins distributed checkpointing.
key_mechanisms: Record channel states on marker receipt

demo.title: Demo — Distributed Consistent Snapshots

title: Incremental Snapshot Chains
description: Stores only the deltas between snapshots to save space. A full snapshot anchors the chain; each link records what changed. Restores walk the chain, trading some restore time for major storage savings.

demo.title: Demo — Incremental Snapshot Chains

title: Snapshot Verification
description: Restores snapshots to staging and runs integrity checks to prove they actually work. An untested backup is a hope, not a plan; verification jobs restore and run smoke tests on schedule. Failures page the team before disaster strikes.
key_mechanisms: Restore to an isolated staging area

demo.title: Demo — Snapshot Verification

title: Cross-Region Snapshot Copy
description: Replicates snapshots to distant regions for disaster recovery. A regional outage must not take the backups with it; cross-region copies complete the 3-2-1 strategy. Copies are encrypted in transit and at rest.
key_mechanisms: Encrypt in transit and at rest
Test restores from the far region

demo.title: Demo — Cross-Region Snapshot Copy

title: Snapshot Encryption
description: Encrypts snapshots at rest with per-snapshot keys so stolen media yields nothing. Keys are managed separately from the data, and rotation does not require re-encrypting old snapshots. It closes the physical-theft vector for backups.
key_mechanisms: Encrypt each snapshot with its own key

demo.title: Demo — Snapshot Encryption

title: Retention Policies
description: Defines grandfather-father-son retention for snapshots: daily sons, weekly fathers, monthly grandfathers. The scheme bounds storage while keeping deep history where it matters. Policies are declared, not remembered.

demo.title: Demo — Retention Policies

title: Restore Drills
description: Practices full restores quarterly to prove recoverability. The drill restores production systems from snapshots into isolation and verifies they run. Teams that drill recover in minutes; teams that do not discover broken backups during disasters.

demo.title: Demo — Restore Drills
